issues.description: Method Rideable.messageOnRide: the problem statement and template call sites expect a parameterless method messageOnRide() returning a string like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" and are invoked as r.messageOnRide(). In the solution repository, Rideable declares messageOnRide(String equipment) (requires a String parameter) and Pig and Seal implement this signature (returning strings that include the equipment). This parameter mismatch prevents code that calls messageOnRide() with no arguments (as shown in the template and described in the problem) from compiling and confuses students which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide signature consistent with the problem statement and template. Option A (preferred): change Rideable to declare String messageOnRide(); and update Pig and Seal to implement a parameterless messageOnRide() returning exactly "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (e.g. "Riding on Pig Doodle"). Update any solution tests or examples accordingly. Option B: if an equipment parameter is intentional, update the problem statement, the UML, and the template Main to call messageOnRide with a String argument and change the expected return format in the specification to include the equipment (document the required call sites and return value).

issues.description: The concept is the Rideable.messageOnRide method. The problem statement / UML and the template/Main expect a no-argument method: Rideable.messageOnRide() : String (problem_statement.md shows {abstract} messageOnRide():String and the template Main calls r.messageOnRide()). The solution repository defines a different signature: Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and the implementations in Pig and Seal implement messageOnRide(String). This parameter-vs-no-parameter mismatch means students cannot directly map the exercise description and provided template code to the solution API and will encounter compilation errors or confusion when following examples in Main.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to match the problem/template by declaring String messageOnRide() (no parameters) in Rideable and implement no-argument messageOnRide() in Pig and Seal to return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Update Pig.java and Seal.java implementations accordingly. Alternatively (less preferred), update the problem statement and template/Main to declare and call messageOnRide(String equipment) consistently; however, aligning the solution to the UML/template avoids breaking the provided Main examples.
